title: AutoRFP vs Responsive (2026): Features, Reviews, Limitations, and Alternatives
summary: AutoRFP vs Responsive compared on AI, pricing, onboarding, and G2 and Gartner ratings, plus who each fits and the AI-native alternative both leave room for. See the verdict.
body_markdown:
If you are shortlisting[RFP software](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-rfp-software) , AutoRFP.ai and Responsive are two names that come up fast. Both automate RFP, security questionnaire, and DDQ responses, both are well reviewed, and both take a different route to the same job.


So the real question is not only which of the two is better, but whether you want a lighter AI-first tool, a response platform with AI added, or an AI-native approach that runs the response end-to-end for you.


Last reviewed: October 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 and Gartner Peer Insights reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing can change, so confirm current figures with each vendor.


## **TL;DR**


- Choose AutoRFP.ai for transparent published pricing, fast AI drafting, unlimited users, and a light setup, if your annual volume fits its per-plan project caps.
- Choose Responsive for enterprise scale, a deep content library, broad integrations, and program-wide reporting, if you can absorb a steeper learning curve and a per-user bill.
- On G2, AutoRFP.ai holds 4.8/5 (about 60 reviews) and Responsive 4.5/5 (1,311 reviews). On Gartner Peer Insights, AutoRFP.ai is 4.8/5 (21 reviews) and Responsive 4.3/5 (55 reviews).
- Both still run on a content library your team maintains and drives step by step. If that upkeep, the project caps, or per-seat pricing is your blocker, an AI-first platform like[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) runs intake, drafting, validation, and governance with[autonomous agents](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-ai-agents-explained) and unlimited users.

## **How AutoRFP.ai works**


AutoRFP.ai provides response management software for[RFPs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/what-is-an-rfp-and-key-components-of-an-effective-rfp) ,[RFIs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfi-request-for-information) , DDQs, and security questionnaires. It uses AI to draft answers from a company's content library with cited sources and confidence scores, auto-saving approved entries for future use. All plans feature unlimited user seats across teams of any size.


## **How Responsive (formerly RFPIO) works**


Responsive, formerly RFPIO, is a response management platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, government bids, and DDQs. It markets itself as AI-first, but the AI sits on top of a content library that owners maintain. Teams use it to organize approved content, route work through reviewer and approval workflows, and connect to a broad set of CRM and document systems.

Inventive AI is built the other way around. Instead of a library your team maintains, it is AI RFP response software where agents handle intake, draft from your connected knowledge, validate the full response, and flag conflicts, while people stay in the loop for approvals. Users are unlimited, and teams go live in days. ## **AutoRFP vs Responsive: features, limitations and reviews**


AutoRFP.ai focuses on AI-assisted drafting using semantic search and browser-based portal auto-filling, whereas Responsive provides broader project tracking, custom review workflows, and extensive enterprise tool integrations.


### **AutoRFP.ai best features**


- AI Response Engine drafts answers from your existing content faster
- Cited sources with a Trust Score on each draft, for quick verification
- Unlimited users on every plan, with no per-seat cost
- Multi-format import and export across Excel, Word, PDF, and web portals
- [SOC 2](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/soc-2-type-2) and ISO 27001 compliance included on all plans
- Integrations across Salesforce, Slack, Teams, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Drive, OneDrive, and Box


### **AutoRFP.ai limitations**


- The interface takes getting used to, and reviewers often lose track of where they left off in a project.
- Getting started is slower without training, because the early learning curve is steep.
- There is no automated content governance, so outdated or conflicting responses have to be caught by a person.
- Free-text and complex source documents are handled poorly and usually need manual cleanup.
- Templates are rigid, which makes adapting formats across different RFPs harder.
- Reporting is limited, with little visibility into the edits contributors make.


### **AutoRFP.ai pricing**


- Scale:[$899 per month](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/autorfp-ai-pricing-features-reviews) , billed annually, for up to 24 projects per year
- Accelerate: $1,299 per month, billed annually, for up to 50 projects per year
- Enterprise: custom pricing for higher volume
- Every plan includes unlimited users, SSO, integrations, and compliance, with no paid add-ons

## **Responsive vs AutoRFP: AI-native feature comparison**


A side-by-side evaluation of how AutoRFP.ai and Responsive apply AI across key workflow areas, including automated answer drafting, repository maintenance, requirements parsing, and review governance.


### **AI agents for end-to-end automation**


AutoRFP.ai: No end-to-end agent. Its AI Response Engine drafts from your content, and a person runs intake, review, and submission. It speeds drafting rather than running the whole response.


Responsive: Partial. Its AI Assistant and agents generate full first drafts across RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, mapping incoming questions to content, while your team still drives intake and review.


### **Go/no-go agent**


AutoRFP.ai: Not a named feature we could verify. Qualification is handled by your team outside the tool.


Responsive: Included. Bid and no-bid fit scoring evaluates an incoming opportunity against your criteria so teams can decide whether to pursue or pass before investing time.


### **Automatic response analyzer**


AutoRFP.ai: Review runs at the answer level through Trust Scores and cited sources, rather than one pass across the full document.


Responsive: Partial, through TRACE Score. It validates individual responses for quality and confidence, which helps reviewers prioritize, but it checks answers one at a time rather than across the whole response.


### **Automatic content governance**


AutoRFP.ai: Partial. The library self-updates from approved responses and runs source checks, including conflict handling, so there is less manual upkeep.


Responsive: Partial. Metadata tagging and TRACE-driven validation support governance at scale, and content can be linked across versions, but it still relies on people to keep the library current and consistent.


### **Integrations**


AutoRFP.ai: Connects to Salesforce, Slack, Teams, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Drive, OneDrive, and Box, plus sourcing platforms such as Ariba, Workday, and Jaggaer, with the connector roadmap still expanding.


Responsive: A broader enterprise layer, with around 30 native integrations and 75+ open APIs, aligning deeply with enterprise CRM, sales enablement, and procurement systems.


### **Analytics**


AutoRFP.ai: Project and content analytics aimed at keeping a focused team's content current and projects on track.


Responsive: Advanced reporting and dashboards built for scale, tracking performance across large teams and many concurrent projects, which suits program-level oversight.


### **User interface**


AutoRFP.ai: Light and fast, though some reviewers report navigation friction, such as finding where they left off in a project.


Responsive: Powerful but denser. Many users find it capable, while others describe the interface as cluttered and say common tasks take extra clicks, with a steeper learning curve.


Two capabilities neither platform fully delivers, agent-driven end-to-end automation and full-document governance with cross-library conflict detection, are the gaps buyers weigh when they look at AI-native tools.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is AutoRFP or Responsive better?


It depends on your team. AutoRFP.ai is better for lean teams that want fast AI drafting, transparent pricing, and unlimited users. Responsive is better for large enterprises that need a deep content library, broad integrations, and program-wide governance. AutoRFP.ai rates higher on G2 (4.8 versus 4.5) and Gartner Peer Insights (4.8 versus 4.3); Responsive has a far larger review base.


### Is Responsive the same as RFPIO?


Yes. Responsive is the current name for the platform formerly known as RFPIO. The rebrand did not change its core RFP and response management capabilities.


### Which is easier to use, AutoRFP or Responsive?


AutoRFP.ai is generally quicker to set up and lighter to run, though some reviewers note interface navigation issues. Responsive is more powerful but denser, and several G2 reviewers describe a steeper learning curve, especially for smaller teams.


### Which has better AI, AutoRFP or Responsive?


Both draft with AI and cite sources. AutoRFP.ai is AI-first and drafts quickly from your content with Trust Scores. Responsive layers AI on its library and validates answers with TRACE Score. Teams that want the AI to run the full response, from reading the RFP to validating the whole document, tend to look at AI-native platforms such as Inventive AI.


### How much do AutoRFP and Responsive cost?


AutoRFP.ai publishes its plans: Scale at $899 per month billed annually for up to 24 projects a year, and Accelerate at $1,299 per month billed annually for up to 50 projects, both with unlimited users. Responsive is quote-based, starting at $10,000 per year for its Emerging Edition, with Growth and Enterprise custom-priced as a platform fee plus user licenses plus add-ons.


### Which is better for enterprise versus a smaller team?


Responsive is built for large, multi-department enterprises with high volume and complex workflows. AutoRFP.ai fits leaner and mid-sized teams that value speed, open pricing, and unlimited users. Teams that want AI-native automation at either size also compare Inventive AI.


### How do I migrate from AutoRFP or Responsive to another tool?


Your response library is exportable from both platforms, so you keep your approved content. AI-native tools can import and de-duplicate that content during onboarding and connect to your live sources, which shortens the switch. Ask any vendor how it imports existing Q&A content and how long go-live takes for a team your size.


### Is there an AI-native alternative to AutoRFP and Responsive?


Yes. A newer category of AI-native platforms, including Inventive AI, takes a different approach: autonomous agents draft from your connected knowledge, keep it current, validate the full response, and flag risks, with unlimited users and go-live in days.
